title: I Took the Bouldering-Wall Reset Log Through Three Open Nights After They Skipped the Holds

parts.text: I arrived for reset at 9:03 p.m. and coach Mira had already skipped the numbered holds. The board said: RESET BEFORE OPEN. HOLDS STAY ON THE LOG. I was twenty-seven, routesetter, holding a clipboard that listed our circuit. Mira shrugged. "Coaches are the wall." I photographed the board, the empty log, and her tape on our start. Then I asked for the reset log. At 9:11 the desk pinged why the circuit still showed last week's holds.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The desk can see last week's holds on tonight's numbered circuit.

social.video_title: They skipped the bouldering reset and left last week's holds — Part 1/3
social.description: Open night, a skipped log, tape on our start. Would you have asked for the reset log?

parts.text: Wednesday they taped our start again. I printed Tuesday's still and put it on the board. Mira called it flow. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. The board now has the still. At 9:16 the desk asked why the reset log was blank two nights running. Mira said optics. Optics is a word coaches use when a circuit exists.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: They taped our start again; the board now has the still.

social.video_title: The reset log was blank two open nights — Part 2/3
social.description: Blank log, a still on the board, tape on our start. Was flow ever a reset?

parts.text: Friday the board added a second line: COACHES ARE NOT THE WALL. Mira ran her own circuit and told the next coach atmosphere was always about optics. I keep our holds on a labeled bin. The reset finally happens before open. Mira brown-bags her tape. The wall finally looks like a log, not a skip. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Coaches are not the wall — Part 3/3
social.description: Second line on the board, holds in a labeled bin, reset before open. Was flow ever last week's circuit?
